name: PKCS#7 SignedData DER parsing and verification
description:
mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der parses a fully attacker-controlled DER byte buffer representing a (detached) PKCS#7 SignedData ContentInfo: it copies the buffer, then walks nested ASN.1 SEQUENCE/SET/OID/INTEGER/OCTET-STRING structures to recover the signed-data version, digest algorithm OID, embedded X.509 certificate(s), and a linked list of SignerInfo entries (issuer/serial, digest/signature algorithm OIDs, signature bytes). Every length, tag, nesting level and OID value in this walk is attacker-controlled, making it a classic memory-safety/parsing-confusion target (pointer arithmetic across nested bounds, allocation/linked-list management for multiple signers, OID comparisons that gate code paths). After parsing, mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_data_verify/mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_hash_verify consume the parsed structure to run a full signature-verification pipeline (hash computation, algorithm-profile checks, mbedtls_pk_verify) against each parsed signer, so a successful parse unlocks a large amount of additional security-relevant code via the resulting object's fields (digest OID, signer list, embedded certificate). mbedtls_pkcs7_free releases the structure, including the dynamically allocated signer linked list and embedded certificate, and must be exercised to find double-free/UAF bugs caused by the parser's error-path cleanup.
- mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der: target/source, builds the mbedtls_pkcs7 object (pkcs7->signed_data, embedded certs, signer list) entirely from the fuzzed buffer; reaches core pkcs7_get_signed_data, pkcs7_get_certificates, pkcs7_get_signers_info_set, pkcs7_get_signer_info.
- mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_data_verify: consumer, runs mbedtls_pkcs7_data_or_hash_verify over the signer list parsed by the target, hashing supplied data and calling mbedtls_pk_verify per signer; exercises certificate-profile checks (mbedtls_x509_profile_check_md_alg/pk_alg) and mbedtls_x509_time_is_past/future on the embedded certificate — additional core beyond the parser itself.
- mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_hash_verify: variant of the verify consumer, feeds a raw hash instead of data-to-be-hashed into the same mbedtls_pkcs7_data_or_hash_verify core as mbedtls_pkcs7_signed_data_verify (alternative, not extra parser coverage, but exercises the hash-length/verify branch differently).
- mbedtls_pkcs7_init / mbedtls_pkcs7_free: lifecycle boilerplate needed around the target (zero the structure before parse, release signer list/cert/raw buffer after); important because parser error paths call mbedtls_pkcs7_free internally and a harness doing parse/free/parse cycles exercises use-after-free and double-free opportunities in the cleanup of partially-built signer lists.
Input space (the DER buffer passed to mbedtls_pkcs7_parse_der drives all of C): the outer ContentInfo can start directly with the SignedData SEQUENCE (bare, OID-less form reached via the MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_UNEXPECTED_TAG "try_data" fallback) or with a full ContentInfo carrying contentType OID — only MBEDTLS_OID_PKCS7_SIGNED_DATA is accepted, so crafting that OID is required to reach the richest code (pkcs7_get_signed_data); the other listed PKCS7 OIDs (DATA, ENCRYPTED_DATA, ENVELOPED_DATA, SIGNED_AND_ENVELOPED_DATA, DIGESTED_DATA) only reach the early rejection path and should be included for negative-path coverage but add little core execution; inside SignedData: the version field (must equal MBEDTLS_PKCS7_SUPPORTED_VERSION=1 to proceed further), the digestAlgorithms SET (number/validity of OIDs recognized by mbedtls_oid_get_md_alg), presence/absence/validity of the optional [0] certificates field (0 vs 1 vs >1 certificates - more than one triggers MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE), the embedded X.509 certificate DER itself (parsed by mbedtls_x509_crt_parse_der, a large nested parser), and the SignerInfos SET (0, 1, or multiple SignerInfo entries, each with its own issuer name/serial/digest-alg/signature-alg/signature fields) — multiple signers exercise the linked-list allocation path in pkcs7_get_signers_info_set. For the verify entries, the certificate's validity period and the compile-time MBEDTLS_PKCS7_ALLOW_WEAK_SIGNATURES setting gate which digest/signature algorithms are accepted.
This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests do with the target stays.
